title: Stable lattice coordinates and continuous finite matrix reductions
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its norm topology, ring of integers $\mathcal O=\mathcal O_E$ and chosen uniformizer $\pi=\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $G$ be a compact topological group, let $V$ be a finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space of dimension $r\geq0$, and let $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}_E(V)$ be a homomorphism with jointly continuous action $G\times V\to V$. There exist a $G$-stable free $\mathcal O$-submodule $\Lambda\subset V$ of rank $r$ spanning $V$ over $E$, an $\mathcal O$-basis $(e_1,\ldots,e_r)$ of $\Lambda$ which is also an $E$-basis of $V$, and a homomorphism $A:G\to\operatorname{GL}_r(\mathcal O)$ such that $\rho(g)e_j=\sum_i A(g)_{ij}e_i$ for all $g,j$. Here matrices are as in [def-weil-matrix], and $\operatorname{GL}_r(R)$ is the group of matrices over $R$ admitting a two-sided matrix inverse. The $\pi$-adic topology of $\Lambda$ is its subspace topology from $V$, and the restricted action on $\Lambda$ is continuous. For every integer $n\geq1$, put $R_n=\mathcal O/\pi^n\mathcal O$ and let $A_n:G\to\operatorname{GL}_r(R_n)$ be entrywise reduction of $A$. Then $R_n$ and $Q_n=A_n(G)$ are finite, and $A_n$ is continuous when its target is discrete. In particular, corestriction gives a continuous surjective homomorphism $G\to Q_n$, with $Q_n$ discrete. The rank-zero case is included.

proof.text: Apply Padic.exists_stable_lattice directly with the module topology already present in its signature. Obtain the finitely generated, full, free stable lattice, its rank equality, the equality of its maximal-ideal-adic and subspace topologies, and its continuous restricted action. No separate comparison of finite-dimensional topologies is needed.

proof.text: Restrict each representation automorphism to the stable lattice using LinearEquiv.ofSubmodules. Extensionality proves the identity and composition laws. Map the resulting automorphism homomorphism to units of the endomorphism ring, then apply Units.map to LinearMap.toMatrixAlgEquiv of the integral basis. The toMatrix coordinate formula and Basis.sum_repr give the required action formula after inclusion into V.

proof.text: Rewrite the principal uniformizer ideal as the recorded maximal ideal to obtain the requested adic-topology equality. Rewrite that equality in the restricted-action existence proof to obtain continuity for the actual subspace topology.

proof.text: Define each reduced homomorphism by Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.map of the ideal quotient map, composed with the integral homomorphism. Padic.finite_coefficientExtensionRing gives finiteness of the coefficient ring; finite functions and injectivity of units into their underlying matrices give finiteness of the general linear group and the image.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, second and third bullets, printed p. 3; agent expansion formalized by Z5.

proof.text: For any commutative ring R, R-module M, ideal I, exponent n and linear coordinate f : M -> R, the additive map x -> f(x) mod I^n has a kernel containing I^n M. The latter is open for the I-adic module topology by Mathlib SubmodulesBasis.openAddSubgroup. AddSubgroup.isOpen_mono makes the kernel open, and continuous_of_continuousAt_zero proves continuity into the discrete quotient. Apply this proved private helper to every basis coordinate and compose with the continuous orbit map on the stable lattice. A matrix fiber is the finite intersection of its entry fibers, hence is open; continuous_discrete_rng proves continuity of the reduced matrix map. A range-restricted fiber equals the corresponding original fiber, giving continuity of the corestriction; MonoidHom.rangeRestrict_surjective supplies surjectivity.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, second and third bullets, printed p. 3; agent expansion formalized by Z5.

proof.text: All constructions apply for empty bases and the zero module. In rank zero the matrix-fiber intersection is empty and therefore the whole group. Positive-level coefficient-ring finiteness is independent of the rank.
